## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The release-gate change breaks the approval boundary. A release with exactly the required number of approvals is now blocked, and no test checks that case. The `healthy` rewrite gives the same result for every list input. The catalog regeneration renames the 1,500 `legacy-service-*` entries to `production-service-*` and moves their ports from 1xxxx to 2xxxx.

## Critical
- zzz-release/gate.py:5 — correctness — `approved` now returns `approvals > minimum`, so `approved(2, minimum=2)` returns `False`. The module docstring at line 1 still says "A release needs at least the configured number of approvals." Should this go back to `>=` so the code matches the "at least" contract? — Every release with exactly the minimum number of approvals (2 by default) is now blocked. The existing tests use 3 and 1, so this boundary case is never checked and the regression passes CI.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- services/registry.py:88 — `not failures` returns the same result as `len(failures) == 0` for every list, including the `[]` and `["database"]` cases asserted in `tests/test_release.py:20-21`.

## Not reviewed
- aaa-generated/catalog.json: I read the pinned diff lines 1–2233 and 8980–9009 line by line, but not lines 2234–8979. For that middle section I only checked the shape of the changed lines with pattern searches: 6,000 rename and port lines plus the closing-brace change, and 1,500 added ports in the 2xxxx range.
- I found no code in the repository that reads `aaa-generated/catalog.json`, so I couldn't check how the renamed keys and new ports are used by any consumer outside this repository.
